anatomy.intro: A low rosette combines fleshy leaves, a growing center and smaller offsets.

parts.function: The thick blade stores water and carries out photosynthesis.
parts.label: Fleshy leaf

parts.function: The narrow colored edge outlines each leaf and may intensify with stronger light.
parts.label: Red margin

parts.function: Successive young leaves expand from the center.
parts.label: Rosette center

parts.function: A daughter rosette can develop beside the original plant.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: Small yellow, urn-shaped flowers hang from long curved stalks above the rosette. Their nodding shape and bright color make the flowering silhouette very different from the tight, nearly stemless leaf crown.

growth.note: Offsets widen the planting while the original crown keeps adding leaves at its center.

stages.text: New central leaves enlarge while older leaves form the outer tiers.
stages.title: Build a rosette

stages.text: Side rosettes can gradually turn one crown into a small group.
stages.title: Add offsets

stages.text: An established rosette may send an arching stalk above its leaves.
stages.title: Raise a flower stalk

habitat.text: Echeveria pulidonis comes from Hidalgo, Puebla and Veracruz in Mexico, in desert or dry shrubland. Thick leaves hold a water reserve within a low, compact rosette. In the shared planter, its short crown needs an open view of the light beneath the taller branching succulents.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria 'Raindrops'
lookalikes.text: Both form blue-green rosettes, but mature 'Raindrops' develops rounded raised bumps; pulidonis has smooth blades with a narrow red outline.

mature.text: Individual rosettes reach about 12 cm across. Basal offsets can broaden the group, while the long flowering stems extend well above the leaf crown.

milestones.text: Acquired at Gerych's Greenhouse in the shared square succulent planter, now tracked as P20 / #2.

nameStory.text: The genus honors Mexican botanical artist Atanasio Echeverría y Godoy. Kew records E. Walther’s publication of the species name in 1972.
